transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, what made me finally call the EAP is that... lately, every little bang in the office just sets me off. Like, if a file drawer shuts or someone drops a coffee mug, it makes me jump really hard. And then my chest just keeps racing way longer than it should over something so small. It's getting pretty distracting, so I figured I needed to talk to someone.
Do you feel anxious or on edge even when there aren't any loud noises or other startling events happening?

Yeah, I do. Actually, when I'm in the office now, I... I just keep checking where my boss is, or where the exits are. I catch myself constantly looking to see if anyone is coming up behind me, even when it's totally quiet and I'm supposed to be focused on my team. It's just this feeling of being on guard all the time.
Have you experienced any episodes where you felt an intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes and included symptoms like palpitations, sweating, or shortness of breath?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. I mean... my heart definitely races when I get startled by a loud noise, like I mentioned, but it doesn't just happen out of nowhere. And I haven't had any sweating or trouble breathing, or that intense fear you're describing. It's more just a constant feeling of being on edge, rather than a sudden episode like that.
Do you have any recurring thoughts or urges that you feel compelled to repeat over and over?

No, not really. I mean, I don't have any thoughts that I feel like I *have* to think about, or anything I feel forced to do over and over. It's really just that constant feeling of being on guard that I mentioned, but nothing like what you're asking about.
Is there something specific that's been causing you a lot of stress lately?

Yeah, it's... well, this has been going on for about two weeks now. It all started after this really intense late-night confrontation I had with my regional boss. Since then, I've just been dealing with all this stress and feeling on edge.
Did the confrontation with your regional boss trigger these feelings of being on guard and startling easily?

Yeah, definitely. Ever since that night, it's like I can't turn it off. When I'm in the office now, I just keep checking where my boss is. I'm always looking at where the exits are, or... or checking to see if anyone is coming up behind me. It's really distracting, honestly, because I'm supposed to be focused on my team, but I'm just constantly watching my back instead.
Have you experienced any nightmares or flashbacks related to the confrontation with your regional boss?

No, I haven't had anything like that. No nightmares about it, and I don't feel like I'm reliving it or having flashbacks. It's really just the being on edge while I'm at work that's the problem. When I go home and go to sleep, I'm fine.
Have you been avoiding your regional boss or certain work situations since the confrontation?

No, not really. I mean, I still have to do my job, so I can't really avoid him or the office. I still go to all the meetings and everything. I just... I'm just really tense when I'm there, you know? But I'm not staying away or anything like that.
How long have you been feeling this way, since the confrontation with your regional boss?
It's been about two weeks now. Yeah, basically ever since that late-night confrontation with him happened, it's just been going on like this.
Have you been having trouble sleeping since the confrontation with your regional boss?

No, my sleep's been okay, actually. Like I said before, once I get home and actually get into bed, I'm fine. I just... I fall asleep normally and sleep through the night. It's really just the daytime stuff at the office that's bothering me.
Have you been experiencing any significant changes in your mood, such as feeling depressed or irritable, since the confrontation with your regional boss?

No, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say I'm depressed or anything. Maybe a little more on edge when I'm at work, but I haven't been snapping at people or feeling really down. It's just that tension I mentioned before.
Do you think your reaction to the confrontation with your regional boss is stronger than you would have expected from yourself?

I don't know, maybe? I mean, I've had disagreements at work before, but this one just... it really got to me. I guess I didn't expect to still be feeling this tense about it two weeks later. So yeah, maybe it is a bit stronger than I'd normally react.
Has your being on edge and constant vigilance at work affected your relationships with your colleagues or your ability to perform your job duties?

Well, I'm still making it in every day, but... yeah, it's definitely affecting my work. I'm just a lot slower with my accounts and making staffing decisions. I've actually had to ask my team to double-check a few things that I would normally just handle on my own without a second thought. It's frustrating. And with performance reviews coming up soon, I'm honestly pretty worried that these mistakes and the slowdown could end up affecting my job.
Are there any specific situations or tasks at work that you've been avoiding since the confrontation with your regional boss?

No, I haven't really been avoiding anything. I mean, I still have to get my work done, so I'm not skipping meetings or putting off certain tasks or anything like that. It's more just... doing the exact same stuff I always do, but just feeling a lot more tense and taking longer to get through it.
Do you think your reaction to the confrontation with your boss would be considered a normal response to a stressful event, or does it feel excessive to you?

I mean... I don't really know what a normal response is supposed to look like. It was a really stressful situation, so of course I was going to be upset. But I guess feeling this keyed up for this long... maybe it is a bit much. I just know it feels awful, whether it's normal or not.
Have you ever had a period of at least six months in your life where you felt consistently anxious or worried about everyday things, even when there wasn't any particular stressor happening?

No, not really. I mean, I get stressed out sometimes, sure, but never for six months straight about just everyday stuff. Usually, if I'm worried, there's a clear reason for it, like a big project at work or something. It's never just out of nowhere for that long.
Do you think your symptoms would improve if the situation with your regional boss were to be resolved?

I'm not really sure. I mean, I guess it would have to help at least a little, right? If the whole thing was just resolved and behind me, it would definitely be a relief. But... I don't know if it would just instantly make me stop feeling so tense all the time. I haven't really thought about it. I'd like to hope it would make things go back to normal, but I just don't know for sure.
Are you avoiding talking or thinking about the confrontation with your regional boss?

No, not really. I mean, I'm not going out of my way to avoid it or anything. I've actually talked about it with a few people since it happened, and I definitely still think about it. So, yeah, I wouldn't say I'm trying to block it out or hide from it.
Have you ever had a time in your life when you felt anxious or worried about everyday things for at least six months, even when there wasn't a specific stressor?

I think you actually just asked me that a minute ago. But, uh, no. Like I mentioned earlier, I haven't. I don't really get stressed for six months straight over just normal everyday stuff. If I'm worried about something, there's usually a clear reason for it.
Have you ever felt anxious or worried about everyday things, like work or finances, for more than six months at any point in your life?

Doctor, I think you just asked me that again. But no, I haven't. Like I said, I don't really get anxious about everyday things for that long. If I'm stressed, there's a reason for it, like what happened with my boss. But just general worry for six months? No, that hasn't happened to me.
